body:
- **Bessembinder (2018, JFE)**: of nearly 26,000 US stocks from 1926–2016, about 58% underperformed one-month T-bills over their lifetimes. Just 1,092 companies (4.3%) accounted for all $35 trillion of net wealth creation; the other 96% collectively matched T-bills. — [ASU W.P. Carey](https://wpcarey.asu.edu/department-finance/faculty-research/do-stocks-outperform-treasury-bills); [Morningstar](https://www.morningstar.com/personal-finance/hendrik-bessembinder-do-stocks-outperform-treasury-bills)
- Global follow-up (64,000+ stocks, 1991–2020): 55.2% of US and 57.4% of non-US stocks underperformed T-bills. US net wealth creation was updated to $47.4 trillion through 2019. ASU lists a version extended to 2025. — [ASU W.P. Carey](https://wpcarey.asu.edu/department-finance/faculty-research/do-stocks-outperform-treasury-bills); [ASU news](https://news.wpcarey.asu.edu/20180917-do-stocks-outperform-treasury-bills)
- **Mauboussin's Base Rate Book** (Credit Suisse, Sept 2016, with Williamson, Morck and Burns) gives base rates for sales growth, gross profitability, operating leverage, margins, EPS growth and CFROI. It documents regression toward the mean and how fast it happens. Sales growth shows low persistence year to year, so start with the base rate (the "outside view") and adjust only with specific reasons. — [Hedge Fund Alpha](https://hedgefundalpha.com/education/michael-mauboussin-the-base-rate-book/); [Book PDF copy](https://josephnoko.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/04/The-Base-Rate-Book-Michael-Mauboussin.pdf); [Moontower summary](https://notion.moontowermeta.com/the-base-rate-book-summary)
- **Kelly criterion** (Kelly 1956; Thorp): practitioners use fractional Kelly (½ or ¼) because the formula assumes known probabilities and payoffs, which investing never has. Half-Kelly reportedly keeps about 75% of growth with about half the volatility. Thorp: full Kelly is "too risky for the tastes of many, perhaps most, investors." — [Wikipedia, Kelly criterion](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_criterion); [GuruFocus, Kelly and capital allocation](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/249988/position-sizes-kelly-criterion-and-prudent-capital-allocation); [Old School Value](https://www.oldschoolvalue.com/investing-strategy/kelly-criterion-investing-portfolio-sizing/)
- Buffett (Q&A transcript): "if you are a professional and have confidence, then I would advocate lots of concentration." The claim that Buffett formally uses Kelly is unverified. — [Wikipedia, Kelly criterion](https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kelly_criterion); [MOI Global, position sizing](https://moiglobal.com/position-sizing-why-conviction-matters-201909/)
- Marks's second-level thinking explicitly asks "what's the probability I'm right?", which is a probabilistic framing. — [Oaktree "It's Not Easy"](https://www.advisorperspectives.com/commentaries/2015/09/24/it-s-not-easy)
- Greenblatt: investors abandon sound strategies after 1–2 bad years, a recency bias that keeps the edge alive for those who stay. — [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/891031/joel-greenblatt-why-people-dont-stick-to-their-strategies)

**Verified price block:** ₹432.25 close 19-Nov-2026 (screener chart).
- Second source: Value Research ₹439.60 NSE on 16-Nov-2026, which equals the screener 16-Nov close of ₹439.60 exactly.
- Upstox ₹431.40 on 2-Nov (10:52 IST) vs screener close ₹434.65: consistent.
- **Discrepancy:** Kotak Neo ₹450.8 on 21-Oct vs screener ₹468.80 (−4%). Kotak may be using a stale or intraday value. I use the screener close.
- Shares ≈ 13.42 cr (TTM PAT 418 / TTM EPS 31.14). **Mcap ≈ ₹5,802 cr. TTM P/E = 13.9x.**

| ₹ cr | FY22 | FY23 | FY24 | FY25 | FY26 | TTM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 2,338 | 3,152 | 4,077 | 5,308 | 6,880 | 7,452 |
| OPM | 11% | 12% | 14% | 15% | 14% | 12% |
| PAT | 65 | 108 | 233 | 329 | 404 | 418 |
| ROCE | 22% | 27% | 35% | 35% | 34% | — |
| Borrowings | 469 | 621 | 667 | 661 | 678 | 766 (Sep-26) |
| CFO | 46 | 143 | 35 | 287 | 643 | — |
| Debtor days | 100 | 75 | 92 | 91 | 92 | — |

| Quarter | Sep25 | Dec25 | Mar26 | Jun26 | Sep26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 1,561 | 1,796 | 1,863 | 1,736 | 2,056 |
| OPM | 12% | 13% | 11% | 12% | 12% |
| PAT | 92 | 110 | 96 | 108 | 104 |

**The annual figure hides a stall.** Revenue grew +32% YoY in Q2, but TTM PAT (₹418 cr) is only +3.5% over FY26 (₹404 cr). Mar-26 PAT was −24% YoY (₹127 cr → ₹96 cr). Q2 FY27 PAT was +12% and was hit by a one-time tax charge and higher interest. OPM has slid from 15% to 12%.

**Shareholding (Dec-24 → Sep-26):**
- Promoter flat at 71.12%. Zero pledge (Ajanma Holdings no-encumbrance declaration, Apr-26).
- DII 15.15% → 5.95% (IPO anchors exiting, a persistent overhang).
- FII 1.0% → 1.85%.
- Institutional direction is **down**.

**Structural story (named cause):**
- Vertically integrated T&D EPC: it makes its own towers, conductors and poles. That is why ROCE (34%) is about double peers like KPIL (18%).
- Customer advances give a negative cash-conversion cycle (about −147 days).
- FY26 CFO of ₹643 cr was 1.6x PAT.
- Order book ₹14,218 cr (1.9x TTM revenue), 93% T&D. The stock has de-rated from ₹632 (Nov-25) to ₹432.

**Bull case:** The price implies only about 6% 10-yr EPS growth for a business growing revenue 30%. If OPM holds at 12% and revenue grows 20% for 3 years, PAT is about ₹700 cr. At 16x that is about ₹11,200 cr, roughly 1.9x. The FY27 inflow guide is above ₹10,000 cr, and October-26 inflow was ₹1,747 cr.

**Risks (blunt):**
- H1 FY27 inflow was only ₹1,638 cr against about ₹3,800 cr executed. **The order book is shrinking** (about ₹16.4k cr → ₹14.2k cr).
- Interest cost is rising and OPM is compressing.
- The DII exit is ongoing.
- There is a related-party acquisition from the promoter (Gactel, ₹10 cr; small) and a Deputy MD resignation.

**Kill criteria:**
- FY27 order inflow below ₹7,000 cr.
- Order book below ₹12,000 cr at Mar-27.
- OPM below 11% for 2 quarters.
- FY27 CFO below PAT.

`person:vijay-kedia` | confidence: **unverified** | tags: india, process, smallcap, multibagger

Mumbai investor from a Kolkata broking family (Kedia Securities); began as a trader and has spoken publicly about early-career losses in the 1990s before shifting to long-term holding. Framework: SMILE - Small in size, Medium in experience, Large in aspiration, Extra-large market potential. Widely cited past winners (media lists; entry prices and multiples not verified here): Atul Auto (three-wheelers, held for over a decade), Aegis Logistics, Cera Sanitaryware, Vaibhav Global, Elecon Engineering, Tejas Networks, Sudarshan Chemical, Precision Camshafts. Folklore: claims that a small early stake in Atul Auto or Aegis turned 1 lakh into crores circulate widely but have no documented entry dates/prices - treat as unverified. Edge: process - concentrated holdings in small companies with ambitious, hungry promoters and a large addressable market, held for years; he meets managements and stresses promoter integrity and 'hunger'. Mistakes: like all small-cap concentrators, several holdings have halved in drawdowns; some later bets (turnaround infra/engineering names) took years to work. Copyable: the SMILE checklist is a reasonable small-cap screen when paired with balance-sheet and governance filters; size each idea so one failure does not matter.

`insight:iima-factor-premiums-india` | confidence: single-source | date: 2026-11-19

Computed by us from IIM Ahmedabad's Fama-French-Momentum data library (Dec-2025 release, survivorship-bias-adjusted monthly long-short factor returns; BSE+NSE stocks via CMIE Prowess DX; micro-caps below 10% of median market cap and sub-Rs1 stocks excluded; RF = 91-day T-bill). Jan-1994 to Dec-2025 (383 months): WML momentum CAGR +10.6% (arith 13.1%/yr, vol 24.5%, t=3.0), max drawdown -53% (Feb-Nov 2000), worst years 2000 -36%, 1998 -32%, 2009 -30% (momentum crashes at market rebounds). HML value CAGR +6.5% (vol 20.4%, t=2.3), max drawdown -59% (1994-2000), worst years 2018 -21%, 2019 -21%; best 2007 +49%, 2021 +39%, 2023 +35%; 2020-25 value CAGR +18.9% (the PSU/cyclical rerating). SMB size CAGR -3.8% (t=-0.85, not significant), max drawdown -86% (1995-2009), negative in 16 of 31 years - the 'small caps always win in India' story is not supported once micro-caps are excluded and the factor is measured long-short. Market factor (excess over T-bills) CAGR only +4.9% vs RF 6.9%, max drawdown -75% (1994-2001): Indian T-bills were a high hurdle. By decade, momentum was strongest 2015-25 (CAGR 12.8%, t=3.0, vol only 14.5%). Lessons: factor premia exist but come with multi-year droughts that test discipline; momentum and value are negatively timed (good diversifiers); size is a tilt, not an edge. Caveats: long-short paper portfolios before costs; data vary between releases.

body:
**1. Promoter loans and promoter-related flows.**
- Loans from promoters (often unsecured, interest-free, classified as quasi-equity) prop up weak balance sheets.
- Loans *to* promoter entities are the classic leak (RHFL "general purpose corporate loans", Gensol).
- Companies Act s.185 restricts loans to directors and their interested entities. s.186 caps loans, guarantees and investments at 60% of capital + free reserves or 100% of free reserves, whichever is higher, unless a special resolution is passed.
- **Test:** loans + advances + investments in group entities / net worth. Above 10% needs a reason; above 25% is a flag.

**2. Inter-corporate deposits (ICDs).**
- These are short-term deposits placed with other companies, often group firms or friendly NBFCs, and frequently shown as "cash-like".
- IL&FS and the 2018 NBFC crisis froze many of them.
- **Test:** ICDs placed / cash + investments, and the counterparty names (RPT note).

**3. Related-party approvals.**
- **SEBI LODR Reg 23:** all RPTs need prior audit-committee approval. Material RPTs (above ₹1,000 cr or 10% of consolidated turnover, whichever is lower) need shareholder approval, and related parties cannot vote.
- **Companies Act s.188** applies to non-arm's-length or non-ordinary-course RPTs.
- Read the AGM notice: a resolution approving "material RPTs up to ₹X cr" with a group company is a forward-looking map of where cash may go.
- **Test:** RPT limits sought / revenue, and how they change year over year.

**4. Promoter pledges and encumbrance** (SEBI SAST Reg 31 disclosures; `tools/nse_fetch.py pledge`). Pledge above 25% or rising is flag #11.

**5. CARO 2020 (Companies (Auditor's Report) Order, 2020).** This annexure to the audit report for most unlisted and listed standalone entities is the single best free forensic document in India. Read these clauses:

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-O:initial-2027-affo-guide-midpoint-4-59-plus`
- **Method:** sector cycle/lead indicator · **P(ours)** 0.40 · **P(base)** 0.50 · resolve by 2027-03-15
- **Evidence:** Q3 2026 release (Nov-2026): AFFO/share $1.12 (+3.7% YoY); 2026 AFFO guidance raised to $4.45–4.46 (from $4.44–4.45); YTD $3.35; reaffirmed $10.0bn 2026 investment volume; 116th consecutive quarterly dividend increase, annualised $3.258 (72.6% payout); raised $472.5m equity at ~$60.49 via ATM forwards, ~18.5m forward shares (~$1.1bn) unsettled. US 10-yr ~4.9–5.1% (Yahoo ^TNX), up from ~4.1% a year earlier.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Sector-cycle lead indicator: net-lease AFFO growth = investment spread × volume. With the 10-year near 5% and the stock (cost of equity) weak, spreads on new acquisitions compress and the company usually guides initial growth conservatively. We lean under even odds for a ≥3% midpoint.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Naive: Realty Income's initial annual AFFO guides have implied ~1–4% growth (from memory, unverified); a ≥3% midpoint is roughly a coin flip.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if the first 2027 AFFO per share guidance range Realty Income publishes (whenever issued, normally with Q4 2026 results) has a midpoint ≥$4.59. If no 2027 guidance is published by 15-Mar-2027, void.
- **Resolution source:** Realty Income Q4 2026 earnings release / supplemental (8-K, EDGAR; realtyincome.com IR)
- **Sources used:** https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/726728/000072672826000056/o-991q32026.htm; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/%5ETNX
- **Confidence of evidence:** single-source

body:
**Operational definitions (fixed before the frame was built):** 1. **Candidates:** every CIK in the `dei:EntityPublicFloat` frames CY2024Q3I … CY2026Q2I (8 instant frames, `sec_fetch.py frames EntityPublicFloat

--taxonomy dei --raw`) with any frame value in a loose band $250M–$15B. 2. **Latest 10-K:** the most recent `10-K`/`10-KT` (amendments ignored) filed 2025-08-23 … 2026-11-23 (a live filer: ≤15 months old), from SEC submissions. **Float** = the `EntityPublicFloat` fact carried by that accession (frame row with the same accession; else companyconcept, summing share classes at the latest date). Keep $500M ≤ float ≤ $10B. 3. **Exclusions by current SIC (submissions):** 6000–6799 (banks, insurers, brokers, REITs 6798, blank checks/SPACs 6770, funds), 4900–4949, 4961, 4991 (utilities), missing SIC. **Biotech without revenue:** SIC 2833–2836 or 8731 and latest-FY revenue on that 10-K (`Revenues` or `RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax`, max) < $10M or untagged. 4. **Order:** frame CIKs sorted ascending (int), `random.Random(20261124).shuffle`, walk from the top. 5. **Stage-2 checks per walked name (in this order; first failure = skip):** a. **Pending merger / scoreability:** any DEFM14A/PREM14A/DEFM14C/PREM14C/SC TO-T/SC 14D9/SC 13E3/Form 25/15 filed by or about the issuer since 2025-11-23, or an 8-K 1.01/2.01 announcing a sale of the company, without a later termination → skip (entity may not exist through 2027-09-30; `decision:live-dd-selection-rules`). b. **8-K 4.02** (non-reliance/restatement) since 2023-11-23 → skip. **8-K 4.01** since 2023-11-23 → read it; skip only if it reports a disagreement or a reportable event (Item 304(a)(1)(iv)/(v)). c. **Going concern / material weakness** in any 10-K or 10-Q filed since 2023-11-23: EDGAR full-text search on the CIK for "substantial doubt" + "going concern" and "material weakness"; every hit is opened and read (risk-factor boilerplate such as "if we identify a material weakness" does not count; an actual conclusion that ICFR/disclosure controls were not effective, or an auditor / management going-concern paragraph, does). d. **Solvency S1 and S5** (definitions of `research_notes/Backtests/solvency_flags_us.md`, code of `tools/backtests/solvency_us/s3_flags.py::snapshot` with T = 2026-11-23, i.e. the latest 10-K's first-reported facts) → skip if either fires. e. **Earnings-surprise avoid window (if computable):** US SUE proxy = seasonal-random-walk EPS surprise (formula of `india_pead/live_tracker.sue_for`) on SEC calendar-quarter EPS frames (diluted, else basic). Bottom quintile = below the 20th percentile of SUE across all frame members for the same calendar quarter. Skip if the latest reported quarter is bottom-quintile and today is within 63 trading days (~91 calendar days) of its 8-K Item 2.02 (or 10-Q) date. Not computable → noted, not a skip. f. **Judgment notes** (not mechanical skips unless they meet (a)–(e)): Chapter 11, delisting notices (8-K 3.01), auditor resignations.
